title_ar: فتوى بخصوص صلاة الجمعة في القرى
title_en: A Fatwa Concerning the Friday Prayer in Villages
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

صلى الله وسلم على رسوله الكريم

الحمد لله وحده

أما بعد فإن صلاة الجُمعة فريضة على المسلمين بالكتاب والسنة والإجماع، ووجوبها معلوم من الدين بالضرورة، فمن أنكره كفر.

أما دليل وجوبها من الكتاب فقول الله تعلى:(يأيها الذين آمنوا إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله..) وقد أجمع المفسرون على أن قوله: (فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله) معناه: امشوا و امضوا إلى سماع الخطبتين وَالصلاة.

وأما دليل ذلك من السنة فمنه ما أخرجه مسلمٌ في الصحيح وأحمد في المسند وغيرهما عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لقوم يتخلفون عن الجمعة: (لقد هممت أن آمر رجلا يصليَّ بالناس ثمَّ أحرق على رجال يتخلفون عن الجمعة بيوتهم).

ومنه ما أخرجه مسلم عن ابن عمر وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهم أنهما سمعا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول على أعواد منبره : (لينتهين أقوام عن ودعهم الجمعاتِ أو ليختمنَّ الله على قلوبهم ثمَّ ليكونن من الغافلين) وقد أخرجه أحمد والنسائي من حديث ابن عمر وابن عباس رضي الله عنهم أيضا.

ومنه ما أخرجه أصحابُ السنن الأربعةُ وأحمد عن أبي الجعد الضمري رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: (من ترك ثلاث جمعٍ تهاوُنًا طبع الله على قلبه) ولأحمد وابن ماجه نحوه من حديث جابر رضي الله عنه، وأخرج نحوه الحاكم من حديث أبي قتادة، و< لفظ > حديث جابر عند النسائي وابن خزيمة والحاكم: (من ترك الجمعة ثلاثا من غير ضرورة طبع على قلبه) وأخرج الطبراني في الأوسط عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: (ألا عسى أحد منكم أن يتخذ الضِّبْنَةَ من الغنم على رأس ميلين أو ثلاثة تأت الجمعة فلا يشهدُها ثلاثا فيطبع الله على قلبه.) والضِبْنة بكسر فسكون: ما تحت يدِك من مال أو عيال.

وأخرج أبو يعلى الموصلي في مسنده عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: (من ترك ثلاث جمع متواليات فقد نبذ الإسلام وراء ظهره)

وهذا موقوف له حكم الرفع لأن مثله لا يقال بالرأي.

وأخرج الطبراني في معجمه الكبير عن عبدالله بن أبي أوفى رضي الله عنهما قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (من سمع النداء يوم الجمعة ولم يأتها ثم سمع النداء ولم يأتها ثلاثا طبع على قلبه فجعل قلب منافقٍ.)

قال العراقي إسناده جيد.

وأخرج ابن ماجه والبزار والدار قطني عن جابر رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: (إن الله افترض عليكم الجمعة في شهركم هذا فمن تركها استخفافا بها وتهاونا ألاَ فلا جمعَ الله له شمله ألاَ ولا بارك الله له ألا و لا صلاة له.) من طريقين في كليهما ضعيف لكن أحدهما يعضد الآخر، والأحاديث في الباب تربو على الخمسين.

وأمَّا الإجماع فقد حكاه كثير من أهل العلم 

ولا يعلم فيه مخالفٌ.

هذا ومن القواعد المسلمة أن الذمة إِذا عمرت بمحقق فلا تبرأ إِلا به.

ولم يرد في النصوص ما يخصص هذا العموم غير حديث طارق ابن شهاب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ( الجمعة حق واجب على كل مسلم في جماعة إلا أربعةً عبدٌ مملوك وامرأةٌ وصبيٌّ ومريض.) أخرجه أبو داود وقال: لم يسمع طارق من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم 

وأخرجه الحاكم موصولا من رواية طارق عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه، وغير حديث جابر رضي الله عنه: ( من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فعليه الجمعة إلا امرأة أو مسافراً أو عبداً أو مريضاً.) أخرجه الدارقطني والبيهقي وفي إسناده ابن لهيعة ومعاذ بن محمد الأنصار وهما ضعيفان.

وغير حديث ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه و سلم قال: ( ليس على مسافر جمعة.) رواه الطبراني في الكبير بإسناد ضعيف.

وبهذا يعلم أن ما يذكره بعض الفقهاء من الشروط التي لم يقم عليها دليل لا يمكن الاعتماد عليه في ترك أمر الله ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ومن ذلك اشتراط العدد فقد نصَّ العلماء على أنه لم يقم عليه دليل يعتمد عليه بل قد ثبت في صحيح مسلم من حديث أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (إذا كانوا ثلاثة فليؤمهم أحدهم.) وهو عام في جميع الصلوات لم يرد ما يخصصه كما قال الحافظ عبد الحق الإِشبيلي المالكيُّ وغيره من كبار الحفاظ.

وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال:( أول جمعة جمّعت بعد جمعة < في > مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مسجد عبد القيس بجُواثى البحرين.) أخرجه البخاري في الصحيح وغيره.

وفي رواية أبي داود: (بجواثى قرية من قرى البحرين)

قلت ومازالت جدران هذا المسجد قائمة إِلى وقتنا هذا وقد صليتُ فيه فوجدته لا يتسع لعشرين رجلا.

ومن ذلك أيضا البناء فقد جمّع أسعد بن زرارة رضي الله عنه في قرية يقال لها هزم النبيت في حرة بني بياضة على ميل من المدينة وكان بناؤهم من جريد وسعف وقصب.

وأقر عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أهل المنازل بين مكة والمدينة على التجميع.

ومن المعلوم أن الذين يشترطون جماعةً تتقرى بهم قرية إنما يقصدون وقت إنشاء القرية، أما بعدَ أن تقرَّتْ القرى فلا يشترطونها لأداء الجمعة.

وعلى هذا فالذي أُراه - والله أعلم – أن أهل القرى القائمة كقرية "إِﮘرم" وغيرها تجب عليهم إقامة الجمعة وهي فرض عين على من حضر يومها من أهل القرية من الذكور البالغين الأحرار الذين لا يشق عليهم حضورُها مشقة عظيمة. والعلم عند الله تعالى.

كتبه محمد الحسن بن الددو. 

------------------

body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

May God bless His noble Messenger and grant him peace.

Praise be to God alone.

To proceed: the Friday prayer is an obligation (farīḍah) upon the Muslims, by the Book, the Sunnah and scholarly consensus (ijmāʿ); and its obligatory status is known of the religion by necessity, so that whoever denies it becomes an unbeliever.

As for the evidence for its obligatory status from the Book, it is the saying of God, exalted be He: {O you who believe, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Friday, hasten to the remembrance of God…} (Sūrat al-Jumuʿah 62:9). The exegetes are agreed that His saying {hasten to the remembrance of God} means: walk and go to hear the two sermons and the prayer.

As for the evidence for that from the Sunnah: among it is what Muslim brought out in the Ṣaḥīḥ, and Ahmad in the Musnad, and others besides them, from Ibn Masʿud, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said of a people who were staying away from the Friday prayer: "I had resolved to order a man to lead the people in prayer, and then to burn down upon men who stay away from the Friday prayer their houses."

And among it is what Muslim brought out from Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with them, that the two of them heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say upon the boards of his pulpit: "Let people desist from their abandoning of the Friday prayers, or God will surely set a seal upon their hearts, and then they will surely be among the heedless." Ahmad and al-Nasaʾi also brought it out, from the report of Ibn Umar and of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them.

And among it is what the authors of the four Sunan, and Ahmad, brought out from Abu al-Jaʿd al-Damri, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever leaves three Friday prayers out of neglect, God sets a seal upon his heart." Ahmad and Ibn Majah have the like of it from the report of Jabir, may God be pleased with him; and al-Hakim brought out the like of it from the report of Abu Qatadah. The ⟨wording⟩ of Jabir's report with al-Nasaʾi, Ibn Khuzaymah and al-Hakim is: "Whoever leaves the Friday prayer three times without necessity (ḍarūrah), a seal is set upon his heart." And al-Tabarani brought out in al-Awsaṭ, from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Might it not be that one of you takes a small holding of sheep a mile or two or three out, and the Friday prayer comes and he does not attend it — three times — and so God sets a seal upon his heart?" Al-ḍibnah, with a kasrah followed by a sukūn, is what is under your hand of property or dependants.

And Abu Yaʿla al-Mawsili brought out in his Musnad, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: "Whoever leaves three consecutive Friday prayers has cast Islam behind his back."

This is a report stopping at a Companion (mawqūf) which has the ruling of one traced to the Prophet (marfūʿ), because the like of it is not said by personal opinion.

And al-Tabarani brought out in his Muʿjam al-Kabir, from Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, may God be pleased with them both, who said: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever hears the call on the day of Friday and does not come to it, then hears the call and does not come to it — three times — a seal is set upon his heart, and it is made the heart of a hypocrite."

Al-Iraqi said: its chain of transmission (sanad) is good (jayyid).

And Ibn Majah, al-Bazzar and al-Daraqutni brought out from Jabir, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "God has made the Friday prayer obligatory upon you in this month of yours; so whoever leaves it, making light of it and out of neglect — then may God not gather his affairs together for him; and may God not bless him; and he has no prayer." By two routes, in each of which there is a weak (ḍaʿīf) narrator, but one of which supports the other. The reports on this subject exceed fifty.

As for scholarly consensus, many of the people of knowledge have reported it,

and no dissenter from it is known.

This said: it is among the accepted legal maxims (al-qawāʿid al-fiqhiyyah) that when a person's liability (dhimmah) has been charged with something established by certainty, it is not discharged except by the like of it.

And nothing has come down in the texts to specify this general ruling (ʿāmm), apart from the report of Tariq ibn Shihab, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The Friday prayer is a right and an obligation (wājib) upon every Muslim in congregation, except four: an owned slave, a woman, a child, and a sick person." Abu Dawud brought it out and said: Tariq did not hear from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Al-Hakim brought it out with a connected chain, from Tariq's narration from Abu Musa al-Ashʿari, may God be pleased with him. And apart from the report of Jabir, may God be pleased with him: "Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, the Friday prayer is incumbent upon him, except a woman, or a traveller, or a slave, or a sick person." Al-Daraqutni and al-Bayhaqi brought it out, and in its chain are Ibn Lahiʿah and Muʿadh ibn Muhammad al-Ansar[i], and the two of them are weak.

And apart from the report of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "There is no Friday prayer upon a traveller." Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Kabir with a weak chain.

By this it is known that the conditions some of the jurists mention, for which no evidence has been established, cannot be relied upon as grounds for abandoning the command of God and of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Among these is the stipulation of a [minimum] number: the scholars have stated explicitly that no evidence that can be relied upon has been established for it. Rather, it is established in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from the report of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When they are three, let one of them lead them." And this is general in scope as to all the prayers, and nothing has come down to specify it — as al-Hafiz Abd al-Haqq al-Ishbili the Maliki said, and others of the great masters of hadith.

And from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: "The first Friday prayer held in congregation, after the Friday prayer ⟨in⟩ the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the mosque of Abd al-Qays at Juwatha in Bahrain." Al-Bukhari brought it out in the Ṣaḥīḥ, and others.

And in Abu Dawud's narration: "at Juwatha, a village among the villages of Bahrain".

I say: the walls of this mosque are still standing to our own day. I have prayed in it, and found that it will not hold twenty men.

Among them [the unfounded conditions] also is a building: for Asʿad ibn Zurarah, may God be pleased with him, held the Friday prayer in a village called Hazm al-Nabit, in the lava field of Banu Bayadah, a mile from Medina; and their building was of palm-stalks, palm-fronds and reeds.

And Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, confirmed the people of the way-stations between Mecca and Medina in holding the Friday prayer.

It is well known that those who stipulate a congregation by whom a village is constituted mean only the time of the founding of the village; but once the villages have been constituted, they do not stipulate it for the performance of the Friday prayer.

Upon this, what I hold — and God knows best — is that the people of established villages, such as the village of "Igrem" and others, are obliged to establish the Friday prayer; and it is individually obligatory (farḍ ʿayn) upon whoever of the people of the village is present on its day, among the free adult males upon whom attending it does not impose a great hardship (mashaqqah). And the knowledge is with God the Exalted.

Written by Muhammad al-Hasan ibn al-Dedew.

------------------

A company of scholars have assented to this fatwa, such as:

1 – Sheikh al-Yadali ibn al-Hajj Ahmad.

2 – Sheikh Mahnadh Baba ibn Ammin.

3 – The learned Sheikh Muhammad Salim ibn Addud.

4 – Sheikh Muhammad ibn Mahfuz ibn al-Mukhtar Fal.

5 – Sheikh and Imam Baddah ibn al-Busayri.

6 – Sheikh Ahmaddu ibn al-Murabit ibn al-Sheikh Ahmadd.

7 – Ustadh Ahmad Ould al-Nini.

8 – Imam Muhammad Mahmud ibn Ahmad Yura.

9 – Sheikh al-Wali Muhammadh ibn al-Wali al-Mukhtar ibn Mahmud.

10 – The learned Hamda ibn Atah.

11 – Sheikh Muhammad Salim ibn Atah ibn Yahzih ibn Abd al-Wadud.

12 – Sheikh Muhammad ibn Ahmad Miskah.

13 – The eminent Sheikh Muhammad Fal ibn Abdullah ibn Abah.

14 – Sheikh Muhammad Abdullah ibn ………

15 – Sheikh Muhammad Abdullah ibn Abd al-Baqi ibn Sid al…

16 – Sheikh Lemrabott Ould Muhammad al-Amin.

17 – Ustadh al-Sheikh ibn al-Sheikh Ahmad.

18 – Sheikh Muhammad Fal ibn Abd al-Latif.

19 – The ascetic Sheikh Ahmaddu ibn Muhammadh Fal (Lemrabott: Maddu).

20 – Sheikh Alla ibn Alla.

flags.arabic: ووجوبها معلوم من الدين بالضرورة، فمن أنكره كفر
flags.context: the opening sentence of the fatwa
options: whoever denies it becomes an unbeliever
whoever denies it has committed an act of unbelief
whoever denies it falls outside Islam
flags.note: EDITORIAL, highest exposure in this record. This is a takfīr statement: denial of the Friday prayer's obligatory status places the denier outside Islam. It is a standard formula of the genre — the classical rule about denying what is 'known of the religion by necessity' — and the Sheikh is applying it to a point of doctrine, not to any person or group named in the record. But in English, on a public page, a scholar's sentence declaring people unbelievers reads very differently from the Arabic and is readily clipped. Style guide section 6 forbids softening, so it has not been softened; the English also avoids the stronger 'apostate', which the Arabic does not say. كفر is a perfect verb: 'has disbelieved'. Whether and how to publish is for Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: من الذكور البالغين الأحرار … إلا أربعةً عبدٌ مملوك وامرأةٌ وصبيٌّ ومريض
flags.context: the ruling's scope, and the report of Tariq ibn Shihab
options: translate 'free adult males' and 'an owned slave' as the Arabic has them
modernise or omit the reference to slavery
flags.note: EDITORIAL. The fatwa's operative ruling is confined to 'free adult males' (الأحرار), and two of the quoted reports except 'an owned slave'. This is the classical vocabulary of the fiqh of the Friday prayer, quoted from hadith, and the conditions have no application today; the Sheikh is not legislating about slavery. It has nonetheless been translated exactly and not modernised away, because silently dropping it would be a falsification. An English page carrying it without editorial framing will be read as a live legal category, which is a reputational exposure the Arabic page does not have. Note too that the exemption of women is reported here as part of the evidence, and the operative ruling is limited to males, which the site should present accurately rather than as a general obligation.

flags.arabic: لقد هممت أن آمر رجلا يصليَّ بالناس ثمَّ أحرق على رجال يتخلفون عن الجمعة بيوتهم
flags.context: the first hadith cited as evidence
options: reproduce the report with the Sheikh's attribution (Muslim, Ahmad) exactly
add the standard discussion of the report
flags.note: EDITORIAL. A prophetic report about burning down the houses of those who stay away from prayer, quoted here as evidence without any of the classical discussion of it (that the Prophet did not act on the resolve, and what the jurists take from it). The English neither adds that discussion nor softens the wording — style guide section 6 forbids both. Note also that the best-known wording of this report concerns the congregational prayer generally; the Sheikh gives it of the Friday prayer, and his attribution is reproduced exactly as he gives it.

flags.arabic: أن الذمة إِذا عمرت بمحقق فلا تبرأ إِلا به
flags.context: the legal maxim that carries the whole argument
options: when a person's liability (dhimmah) has been charged with something established by certainty, it is not discharged except by the like of it
when the liability is occupied by a certain obligation, it is not cleared except by certainty
once an obligation is established with certainty, only certainty can discharge it
flags.note: The hinge of the argument, and genuinely ambiguous in the Arabic: the pronoun in فلا تبرأ إلا به may refer to 'something certain' (the same obligation) or to 'certainty' (an equally certain discharge). The second reading is the usual sense of the maxim in the uṣūl works and is what the fatwa needs — an obligation established by certain evidence cannot be set aside by conditions resting on no evidence. Rendered so as to keep both readings open. dhimmah in this technical sense (a person's capacity to bear obligations) is not in the glossary and is a candidate for addition; it is unrelated to dhimmah as a status of protection.

options: its chain of transmission (sanad) is good (jayyid)
its chain is sound
its chain is of good standing
flags.note: GRADING PRECISION. jayyid is a grading term distinct from the glossary's ḥasan ('good') and from ṣaḥīḥ ('sound'); the masters do not use them interchangeably, and jayyid is generally understood at or near ṣaḥīḥ. The English gives 'good (jayyid)' with the Arabic attached so that it cannot be confused with a ḥasan grading, and the attribution to al-Iraqi is kept exactly. jayyid is a candidate for the glossary.

flags.arabic: و< لفظ > حديث جابر … بعد جمعة < في > مسجد رسول الله
flags.context: two places in the citation of evidence
options: reproduce the angle brackets as marks of an editorial insertion in the source
silently incorporate the words
omit them
flags.note: SOURCE (house rule 11). The angle brackets are in the served page and mark words inserted by whoever prepared the text — not by the Sheikh, and not by this translator. They are carried into the English as angle brackets so the reader can see the insertion. Both are needed for the sense, which is presumably why they were supplied.

flags.arabic: 14- الشيخ: محمد عبد الله بن ........ / 15- الشيخ: محمد عبد الله بن عبد الباقي بن سيد ال...
options: reproduce the truncations visibly and flag
omit the incomplete entries
complete the names
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11), and a serious one: two of the twenty endorsing scholars are named only in part, the text breaking off in dots. These are attestations by living or recently living Mauritanian scholars to a fatwa, so an incomplete or wrongly completed name attributes a legal position to a person. The lacunae are left visible and nothing has been supplied. THE WHOLE LIST needs verification before publication: the romanisations given are conventional renderings of Mauritanian names (Ould, Lemrabott, Ahmaddu, Muhammadh, Yahzih, Addud) whose customary English spellings vary considerably, and several are well-known figures whose names should be spelled as they themselves spell them.

flags.arabic: وقد سلم هذه الفتوى كوكبة من العلماء مثل
flags.context: the heading of the list of endorsements
options: a company of scholars have assented to this fatwa
a galaxy of scholars have conceded this fatwa
a group of scholars endorsed this fatwa
flags.note: سلّم in this construction is 'conceded, assented to, accepted without dispute', which is weaker than 'signed' or 'endorsed' — the record does not say these scholars signed anything. The English keeps the weaker sense deliberately. كوكبة is literally a constellation or galaxy; 'a company' avoids an English register the Arabic does not carry. The word مثل ('such as') also shows the list is not represented as complete.

flags.context: the village named in the operative ruling
options: the village of "Igrem"
the village of "Egrem"
the village of "Ikrem"
flags.note: A Mauritanian place name written with the Maghrebi gāf (ﮘ), which the Arabic alphabet as normally printed has no letter for; the romanisation is a guess at the vowels. This is the only place in the fatwa that ties it to a particular locality, and the fatwa appears to have been written for a specific dispute in that village about whether it might hold the Friday prayer. The Sheikh's office should confirm the spelling.

flags.arabic: ولم يرد في النصوص ما يخصص هذا العموم … وهو عام في جميع الصلوات لم يرد ما يخصصه
flags.context: the structure of the legal-theory argument
options: keep the takhṣīṣ vocabulary visible: a general ruling (ʿāmm) and what specifies it
paraphrase as 'exceptions'
flags.note: The argument is conducted in the vocabulary of legal theory, not of exceptions: a general text (ʿāmm) stands until a specifying text (mukhaṣṣiṣ) is produced, and the Sheikh reviews the candidates one by one and finds them weak or inapplicable. Style guide section 1 requires the reasoning chain to be preserved rather than compressed into its conclusion, so the English keeps 'general in scope' and 'specify' throughout rather than saying 'exceptions'.

flags.arabic: فقول الله تعلى / والدار قطني / معاذ بن محمد الأنصار
options: reproduce the source's spellings in body_ar and translate by the evident sense
correct them
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECTS (house rule 11), orthographic only: تعلى for تعالى; الدار قطني written as two words; الأنصار for الأنصاري; امرأة written without hamzah in the list of endorsers' names. The English marks the missing yāʾ of al-Ansari with a bracket and otherwise translates by the evident sense. Nothing has been silently repaired.

translator_notes: A complete formal fatwa: a ruling stated, evidence from the Qur'an, from the Sunnah report by report with collections named, from consensus, then a legal maxim, then the examination and rejection of the specifying evidence and of the conditions some jurists add, then historical precedents, then the ruling applied to a named village, then the signature and twenty endorsements. Nothing has been summarised and no paragraph skipped.

فريضة and وجوب and واجب and فرض عين are all rendered by the fixed mappings ('obligation', 'obligatory status', 'obligation (wājib)', 'individually obligatory'). The Sheikh writes in his own Maliki voice, so farḍ and wājib are not distinguished; no Hanafi position is being reported here.

أخرج is rendered 'brought out' throughout, the technical sense of a compiler publishing a report with his own chain, rather than 'narrated' (روى), which the fatwa also uses separately and which is rendered 'narrated'.
جمّع / التجميع is the technical verb for holding the Friday prayer in congregation, distinct from simply praying; rendered 'held the Friday prayer' / 'holding the Friday prayer'.

تتقرى بهم قرية: 'by whom a village is constituted' — the Maliki condition that a settled community exists, which the Sheikh reads as a condition on founding a village, not on praying in one that already exists. This reading is the pivot of the whole fatwa.
الضِّبْنة is glossed by the Sheikh himself in the text, with its vocalisation; both his gloss and the vocalisation are kept.
حرة بني بياضة is a lava field (ḥarrah) near Medina; rendered literally.
The Qur'anic rendering is interpretive and is not a substitute for the Arabic.
